fact: WebSocket bridge must handle both NDJSON (Claude Code) and JSON-RPC (Codex) protocols
recommendation: Always test protocol changes against both backends

fact: Session state persists to $TMPDIR/vibe-sessions/ as JSON and survives server restarts
recommendation: Test session recovery after server restart when changing session-related code

fact: Every frontend component must have .test.tsx with render + axe a11y scan
recommendation: Create test file alongside component, include toHaveNoViolations()

fact: Think before coding: state assumptions explicitly, surface tradeoffs, ask when unclear instead of picking silently
recommendation: Before any non-trivial change, name your assumptions, present alternatives if multiple interpretations exist, and stop to ask if something is genuinely ambiguous. Don't hide confusion behind plausible-looking code.

fact: Simplicity first: write the minimum code that solves the problem; no speculative abstractions, flexibility, or error handling for impossible cases
recommendation: If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite. Avoid abstractions for single-use code. Ask 'would a senior engineer call this overcomplicated?' — if yes, simplify before submitting.

fact: Surgical changes: every changed line should trace directly to the user's request; don't 'improve' adjacent code, comments, or formatting
recommendation: When editing existing code, match its style even if you'd write it differently. Only remove imports/vars that YOUR change orphaned. Mention unrelated dead code, don't delete it unprompted.

fact: Goal-driven execution: transform tasks into verifiable success criteria so the loop can close itself
recommendation: Convert imperative requests into declarative goals: 'add validation' → 'write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass'. For multi-step work, write the brief plan with a verify step per item before starting.
